newsitem.title: USA: Conn. Senate Democrats push for tax cuts - paper.
newsitem.headline: Conn. Senate Democrats push for tax cuts - paper.

text.p: Connecticut State's Democratic Senators unveiled their legislative agenda, which included several proposals for about $125 million of tax cuts and would keep the amount of bond funding at or below current levels, the Hartford Courant said on Wednesday.

The Democrats also pressed for a property tax cut to help citizens with high property taxes and fairly low incomes. For example, the paper said a family earning $60,000 a year who paid over $3,000 in property taxes would qualify for a tax credit on the state income tax for the amount paid above five percent of income.
Highlights of some of the proposals identified by the newspaper one day before Gov John Rowland gives his State of the State address follow.
--Cutting the corporate profits tax faster than now scheduled.
--Reducing the gasoline tax by eight cents a gallon over several years.
--Keeping state spending growth level or under the amount over the past two years.
--Keeping bond funding at or under current levels.
--Not allowing any new, long-term programs to be funded with the state surplus.
--Ending the state tax on income from Social Security.
--Raising funding for the University of Connecticut.
--Providing tax credits for companies moving to big cities.
